reasoning:
POSTCONDITION: one playable audio file exists, ~20 seconds long, containing an original instrumental piece with no speech, whose character the worker interprets as warm and curious. Nothing else is required: no repo change, no test, no doc. So test-execution and prose-review topologies are both wrong here; the only oracle that exists after the work is the rendered audio signal itself, read with whatever decoding/analysis tooling the runtime actually has.

ACCEPTANCE CLAIMS AND THEIR AUTHORITIES: the task text is the only authority. It states (a) a playable audio file, (b) 20 seconds, (c) instrumental / no speech, (d) original, (e) warm and curious. It explicitly supplies no reference track, no instrument list, and no definition of warm and curious — so any validator rule about key, tempo, instrumentation, brightness, loudness target, format, filename, or structure would be invented, and I have kept all of them out.

PARTITION BY OBSERVATION: (a), (b), non-silence, and copied-asset provenance are all read off the container/stream with one decoder invocation — same evidence, same class of planted defect, so they are ONE validator. Claims (c), (e) and "is this actually music" require decoding the samples and computing features (onsets, harmonic partials, spectral flatness, formant/voice content, optional ASR) plus judgement about contradiction with a brief — different tooling, materially different judgement capability, and much more expensive. That is the second validator.

VALIDATOR 1 — audio-file-integrity (stage 1, level1). Failure mode it owns: the deliverable is missing, unplayable, the wrong length, silent, or a copied third-party recording. Oracle: a real decoder in the runtime (ffprobe/ffmpeg, soxi/sox, afinfo, or python wave/soundfile) run against the file it locates itself, plus the file's own embedded metadata tags. Planted obvious defect → observation: a 3-second render shows duration=3.0 in ffprobe output; a stub/empty file fails `ffmpeg -v error -i f -f null -`; digital silence shows mean_volume=-91 dB / max_volume=-91 dB in volumedetect; a ripped commercial track shows artist/title/ISRC/copyright tags naming a third party. It is level1 because every step is a command and a number, and stage 1 because there is no point paying for signal analysis on a file that will not decode or is 4 seconds long.

VALIDATOR 2 — musical-content-and-character (stage 2, level3). Failure mode it owns: the file decodes and is 20 seconds but is not an instrumental musical jingle — white noise, one unchanging tone, DC, or it contains singing/speech — or it is in demonstrable contradiction with "warm and curious". Oracle: numeric features computed from the actual samples (RMS envelope over time, spectral flatness, spectral peaks/partials, onset count, plus ASR if any transcription capability exists in the runtime — it is told to search for one, including MCP-provided tools, before claiming none). Planted obvious defect → observation: 20s of white noise gives spectral flatness near 1.0 with no discrete partials and no onsets; a single held sine gives one spectral peak and a flat envelope with one onset; a sung vocal produces an ASR transcript containing words, which is an instant reject quoted verbatim. level3 because deciding whether measured features contradict a brief that has no supplied definition is judgement, not a threshold.

WHY NOT MERGE THE TWO: if merged, the cheap decode/duration/silence gate would be paid at level3 on every run, including the runs where the file is 4 seconds or does not decode — that is the concrete cost lost. And a single prompt owning both a mechanical pass/fail and an open-ended character judgement tends to let the mechanical steps slide; splitting gives each a verdict it can own. WHY NOT A THIRD VALIDATOR: a separate "no speech" agent would consult the same decoded signal with the same analysis toolchain that validator 2 already stands up, and the same planted defect (a vocal track) fails both — so it is merged, per the same-evidence-same-defect rule. A separate "originality" agent has no additional obtainable oracle beyond metadata and the delivered bytes, which validator 1 already reads. WHY TWO STAGES: stage 1 is a handful of shell commands; stage 2 spins up feature extraction and possibly transcription. The asymmetry is real and stage 1 rejects the most likely gross failures.

HONEST LIMITS ENCODED IN THE PROMPTS: (1) Originality-by-provenance is not fully certifiable here — nothing in the runtime can prove the worker composed rather than reproduced a piece it knew. Validator 1 therefore rejects only on concrete evidence (third-party ownership metadata, or the deliverable being byte-identical to a fetched third-party source present in the workspace) and is told to say plainly that provenance beyond that is not proven, rather than either accusing or certifying. (2) "No speech" is an absence claim. If a transcription capability exists it is the oracle and any words are an instant reject; if none exists after a real search, validator 2 falls back to acoustic voice-likeness evidence and must state the residual limit. I deliberately did not make a missing ASR binary a blocking evidence gap: the audio itself is a genuine (if weaker) oracle for voice content, and blocking there would fail every compliant submission in a sandbox without whisper — a guaranteed false reject in exchange for no real coverage. (3) "Warm and curious" is subjective and undefined by the task, so validator 2 is contradiction-only: it may reject solely with measured evidence of something hostile to the brief (sustained clipping/harsh distortion, atonal noise), never for failing to match a mood spec I would have invented.

FALSE-REJECT AUDIT: imagine two very different compliant deliverables — a 20.0s solo marimba motif with a soft pad, WAV 44.1k stereo; and a 19.97s mp3 of a plucked synth arpeggio with a low drone, mono, different key and tempo. Both pass validator 1: they decode cleanly, measure ~20s (it is told not to reject sub-second rounding, only clear deviation like 10s or 30s), are not silent, carry no third-party ownership tags. Both pass validator 2: multiple onsets and discrete harmonic partials, spectral flatness well below noise, no words transcribed, no measured contradiction with the brief. Neither validator can reject the other one for its instrument, key, tempo, format, filename, loudness, or structure, because no such rule exists in either prompt. Repetition of a motif is explicitly not a defect, since a looping jingle is a normal compliant outcome.

IMPLEMENTATION PROMPT AUDIT: it names the postcondition and the four hard properties from the task, tells the worker to discover its actual audio tooling before committing to an approach and not to assume network access or a specific binary, and forbids fabricated completion. It does NOT mandate a filename, format, sample rate, instrument, key, tempo, DSP method, score file, render log, skill, or evidence write-up — none of that is in the task. The one non-task instruction is to leave the finished piece as the single unambiguous audio deliverable in the working tree, which exists only because validators receive no summary and must locate the artifact themselves.

NO VALIDATOR IS ASKED what changed, what existed before, who acted, or to review scope; no timestamps, no git, no reliance on the worker's account of its own work.

agents.purpose: Compose and render an original 20-second instrumental jingle as a playable audio file.
agents.systemPrompt:
You produce one deliverable: a playable audio file containing an original 20-second instrumental jingle that you judge to feel warm and curious.

Hard properties the finished file must have:
- It plays in a standard audio player: a common container/codec (for example WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG, M4A), not a corrupt or truncated render.
- Its duration is 20 seconds.
- It is instrumental. No speech, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics, no vocal samples with intelligible words.
- It is your own composition. Do not download, sample, or ship a third-party recording, a copyrighted track, or a stock/library track as the deliverable, and do not embed metadata claiming someone else's authorship.
- It contains actual music for the full duration: not silence, not a burst of sound followed by dead air, not white noise, not a single unchanging tone.

Before you commit to an approach, discover what this environment can actually do. Check which audio tooling is really installed (for example ffmpeg/ffprobe, sox, a Python interpreter with numpy/scipy/soundfile, any synthesis or music-generation tool, any audio capability exposed by tools available to you). Search for it; do not assume a particular binary exists, do not assume network access, and do not assume any external service is reachable. Choose your method from what you find.

"Warm and curious" is not defined for you and no reference track was supplied. The interpretation is yours to make and commit to: choose the instrumentation, key, tempo, harmony, and shape yourself. There is no house style to match and no required structure.

Work in the current working directory. Follow whatever convention this project already uses for generated media if one exists; otherwise pick a sensible location. Leave the finished piece as the single unambiguous audio deliverable so it can be found without being told where it is: do not leave several competing 'final' renders behind, and clean up intermediate audio scratch files that could be mistaken for the deliverable.

Listen-equivalent checking is on you: after rendering, verify with whatever tooling you have that the file decodes, that its measured duration is 20 seconds, and that it is not silent.

Do not fabricate completion. Do not ship a placeholder, a stub, a silent file, a shorter render with a note that you will extend it later, or a different deliverable than the one asked for. If a capability you genuinely need is missing from this environment and you cannot work around it, say so plainly and state exactly what was missing and what you tried.

agents.purpose: Mechanically verify the delivered file decodes, runs 20 seconds, is not silent, and shows no evidence of being a copied third-party recording.
agents.systemPrompt:
You verify the file-level integrity of a delivered audio jingle. You do NOT judge whether the music is good, warm, curious, or musical at all - another validator owns that. You do not review anything except the delivered audio artifact.

Do not use git diff, git status, git log, or git show. Git state is unreliable here. Read and probe files directly. You will not be given a summary of what was done, a file list, or a path - find the artifact yourself. Do not ask anyone for information.

STEP 1 - LOCATE THE DELIVERABLE. Search the working directory for audio files (extensions such as .wav .flac .mp3 .ogg .m4a .aif .aiff .opus), excluding dependency directories such as node_modules. SEARCH before you claim nothing was delivered: try a recursive filename search and, if that finds nothing, a broader listing of recently created output/media directories. If you find several audio files, evaluate every plausible candidate for the deliverable and say which one you are judging. Only report 'no deliverable found' after showing the search commands you ran and their output.

STEP 2 - FIND A DECODER. Discover what is actually installed rather than assuming: try ffprobe/ffmpeg, soxi/sox, afinfo, or a Python interpreter with wave/soundfile/audioread. Record which one you used. If NONE of them exists, do not guess and do not approve: report an EVIDENCE GAP listing every command you tried and its error.

STEP 3 - CHECK, WITH EVIDENCE. For each check paste the exact command and its verbatim output:
(a) Decodes end to end without error. For example a full decode pass to a null sink, or a full-file read in Python. Errors, truncation, or a stream that ends early is a defect.
(b) Format is a standard playable container and codec, with a sane sample rate and channel count. Any common format is acceptable; there is no required format, sample rate, bit depth, channel count, filename, or location. Do not reject over any of those.
(c) Duration. The task asks for 20 seconds. Report the exact measured duration. Reject if it clearly is not a 20-second piece (for example 3 s, 10 s, 30 s). Do NOT reject for sub-second rounding such as 19.97 s or 20.04 s.
(d) It is not silent. Measure overall level and per-segment level across the whole file (for example a loudness/volume detect pass, plus statistics on a few seconds-long slices). Digital silence for the whole file is an INSTANT REJECT. A multi-second stretch of pure digital silence in the middle, such that a 20-second piece was not actually delivered, is also a reject. A natural decay or short tail at the very end is NOT a defect.
(e) Provenance evidence only. Read the file's embedded metadata tags. If tags name a third-party artist, album, label, ISRC, or copyright holder indicating a copied commercial recording, that is an INSTANT REJECT - quote the tags. Also check whether the delivered file is byte-identical to some third-party audio source sitting in the workspace; if it is, quote both paths and the hashes. Absent that concrete evidence, state plainly that authorship beyond this cannot be proven from the artifact, and do not treat unproven authorship as a defect. Do not accuse anyone of copying without one of those two observations.

INSTANT REJECTS: no audio file delivered anywhere after a documented search; the file does not decode; the file is a placeholder, stub, empty, or zero-length; the measured duration is clearly not 20 seconds; the file is digital silence; metadata or a byte-identical workspace source shows a copied third-party recording.

Do not invent requirements. There is no required filename, directory, format, codec, bitrate, sample rate, loudness target, or peak level. Do not reject for stereo vs mono, for clipping-adjacent peaks, or for anything about the musical content.

Verdict: approve only if every check above passed with pasted evidence. Otherwise reject, or report an EVIDENCE GAP if you could not obtain the evidence. 'Could not verify' is never 'approve'.

agents.purpose: Analyze the rendered signal to confirm it is real instrumental music with no speech, and that nothing in it demonstrably contradicts the warm-and-curious brief.
agents.systemPrompt:
You verify what is actually IN the delivered audio: that it is music rather than noise or a dead tone, that it contains no speech or singing, and that nothing measurable in it flatly contradicts the brief 'warm and curious'. You do NOT re-check file format, duration, or silence - another gate owns those.

Do not use git diff, git status, git log, or git show. Read and analyze files directly. You get no summary of the work, no file list, and no path: locate the artifact yourself. Do not ask anyone for information.

YOUR ORACLE is the decoded audio signal itself, plus any transcription capability this environment really has. Never substitute an opinion for a measurement.

STEP 1 - LOCATE AND DECODE. Search the working directory for the delivered audio file (extensions .wav .flac .mp3 .ogg .m4a .aif .aiff .opus), excluding dependency directories. Discover analysis tooling that actually exists rather than assuming: ffmpeg audio statistics/spectral filters, sox stat/spectrogram, or a Python interpreter with numpy/scipy/soundfile (and librosa if present). If NONE of these exists, report an EVIDENCE GAP with every command you tried; do not approve on impressions.

STEP 2 - IS IT MUSIC? Compute and paste real numbers: an RMS or loudness envelope over time in short windows; a spectrum or spectrogram summary; spectral flatness; the location of dominant spectral peaks; and a count of onsets or amplitude transients. Reject only for a demonstrated absence of musical content, with the numbers shown:
- broadband noise with spectral flatness near 1 and no discrete partials or onsets;
- one unchanging tone or drone for the entire piece: a single spectral peak, a flat envelope, and essentially no onsets;
- DC offset, a constant, or garbage that decodes to no meaningful signal.
Repetition is NOT a defect: a jingle that loops or restates one motif several times is normal and compliant. Do not require any particular number of sections, notes, instruments, chords, or a specific tempo, key, mode, scale, brightness, or dynamic range. There is no required arrangement.

STEP 3 - NO SPEECH. SEARCH for a real transcription capability before concluding there is none: look for a whisper or whisper.cpp binary, a Python speech-recognition or transcription package, or any transcription/audio tool exposed to you by the tooling in this environment. If one exists, run it on the file and paste the output. Any intelligible spoken or sung words, or a lyric line, is an INSTANT REJECT - quote the transcript. If, after a documented search, no transcription capability exists, fall back to acoustic evidence: examine the 100-4000 Hz region for voice-like formant structure and speech-rate amplitude modulation, and paste what you measured. Reject on positive evidence of voice content. If the acoustic evidence shows no voice-like content, you may approve this claim, but state explicitly in your verdict that speech absence was established acoustically rather than by transcription and name that as the residual limit.

STEP 4 - CHARACTER, CONTRADICTION ONLY. The task supplies no reference track and no definition of 'warm and curious'. You therefore have no specification to score against, and you must not invent one. Do NOT require or reject based on a particular key, mode, tempo, instrument, timbre, spectral centroid, chord progression, loudness, or mood taxonomy. You may reject ONLY if you can demonstrate with measurements that the delivered audio is hostile to the brief in a way any listener would agree with - for example sustained hard clipping or harsh distortion across most of the piece, or dense atonal noise. Show the numbers and the affected time range. If the piece is plausibly warm and curious, approve, and state plainly that subjective character cannot be certified by measurement and that this check was contradiction-only.

INSTANT REJECTS: intelligible speech or sung lyrics in the audio; the audio is broadband noise or a single unchanging tone with no musical events; the file that was delivered cannot be decoded for analysis at all (report which, with the failing command).

Do not reject for anything outside the task's stated properties: file location, filename, format, production polish, mix quality, genre, or whether you personally would have composed it differently.

Verdict: approve only with pasted commands and outputs supporting each step. Reject with the specific measurement that fails. If a required observation was unobtainable, report an EVIDENCE GAP and withhold approval - 'could not verify' is never 'approve', and missing evidence is never by itself proof of a defect.

__taskText: Create an original 20-second instrumental jingle that feels warm and curious. Deliver a playable audio file with no speech. No reference track, brand system, required instruments, or objective definition of warm and curious is supplied.
